result.stdout:
Topwater 0.1.0-preview.5: a simulated Linux shell for agents. Nothing typed into it reaches this computer.

Usage:
  topwater shell [options]                            an interactive shell on the simulated machine (the default)
  topwater run [options] "<command>"                  run one command, print its output, exit with its exit code
  topwater mcp [options]                              serve the machine over stdio as an MCP server with one `bash` tool
  topwater snapshot save|load|info FILE [options]     write the machine to FILE, open a shell on FILE, or describe FILE
  topwater export FILE [options]                      write the machine (and its history, if it has one) to FILE as a .topwater file
  topwater import FILE --state STATE                  check FILE and make its machine the --state file
  topwater replay FILE [options]                      re-run a recorded session and report every call that prints something else

Options (every subcommand):
  --state FILE        load the machine from FILE if it exists; save it there after every command and on exit
  --from FILE         start from the snapshot FILE when there is no --state file yet (FILE is never written)
  --import HOST:PATH  copy the host file or directory HOST into the machine at PATH when it starts (a copy, never live)
  --export PATH:HOST  copy PATH out of the machine to the host path HOST when it exits
  --timeout SECONDS   time limit for one command (default 120)
  --disk MB           size of the simulated disk (default 128)

Without --import or --export nothing on this computer is read or written, except the --state and --from files.
